sec: The cirrhotic sinusoid: diagram labels · p1001

items.q: Match the cirrhotic-sinusoid diagram events of p1001 to the structures — 1) Deposition of collagen  2) Activation  3) Constriction  4) Defenestration … A) Sinusoids  B) Hepatic stellate cells  C) Space of Disse  D) Sinusoidal lumen/fenestrae
items.exp: Diagram labels: deposition of collagen in space of Disse; activation of hepatic stellate cells; constriction of sinusoids; defenestration of sinusoids. (Book p1001)

items.q: In cirrhosis, collagen deposition in the hepatic sinusoid occurs in the:
items.exp: The diagram labels ‘Deposition of collagen in space of Disse’. (Book p1001)

items.q: Which cell is labelled as activated in the cirrhotic sinusoid of p1001?
items.exp: ‘Activation of hepatic stellate cells’ is labelled in the cirrhotic panel. (Book p1001)

items.q: ‘Fenestrae of the sinusoidal endothelium are preserved in cirrhosis.’
opts: False — fenestrae are lost only in Budd–Chiari
True, but only in the pericentral zone
items.exp: The cirrhotic panel labels ‘Defenestration of sinusoids’ and the summary line reads ‘Disappearance of fenestration in cirrhosis’. (Book p1001)

items.q: In a cirrhotic liver, the direct mechanical mechanism by which regenerating nodules raise portal pressure, as drawn on p1001, is:
opts: Compression of sinusoids by nodules and fibrous septae
Stenosis of hepatic veins by nodules
items.exp: ‘Nodule and fibrous septation compress sinusoids → leads to ↑ portal pressure → ↑ splenic vein pressure’. (Book p1001)
